---
title: "Enhancing YouTube Data Donations With Platform Metadata"
---

This project demonstrates how donated YouTube watch histories can be linked with video-level platform metadata to create enriched exposure histories.

The workflow combines mock Google Takeout-style data with a metadata table in order to show what researchers can learn once watch events, search histories, subscriptions, metadata, and availability signals are joined around the YouTube `video_id`.

## What This Adds

Raw watch histories tell us that a participant started watching a video at a particular time. After enrichment, the same watch event can also carry:

- video duration, channel, popularity fields, format, and availability status;
- whether the watch closely followed a donated YouTube search;
- whether the video came from a donated subscribed channel;
- whether the event was a Short or Long;
- whether the event happened during the configured day or night period;
- whether later metadata errors indicate an unavailable or problematic-view signal.

## Workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["Mock Google Takeout data<br/>watch, search, subscriptions"] --> B["Clean donated histories"]
  C["YouTube metadata<br/>yt-dlp or demo fixture"] --> D["Video-level metadata table"]
  B --> E["Event-level enriched watch table"]
  D --> E
  E --> F["Search, subscription,<br/>Shorts/Longs, day/night,<br/>problematic-view indicators"]
  F --> G["Showcase tables and figures"]
```

## Recommended Entry Point

Start with [Notebook 05](scripts/05_demonstrate_enriched_exposure_measures.html). It shows what the enriched data looks like and produces compact figures that demonstrate the article-facing value of the method.

Then use [the notebook guide](notebooks.html) to inspect the earlier cleaning, scraping, and linking steps.

## Mock Data

The repository contains scrambled mock Google Takeout-style data in `data/mock_takeout`.

The mock data include three fictional donors:

- Alma
- Beata
- Carmen

Each donor folder contains small watch-history, search-history, and subscription files with the same broad structure as a YouTube Takeout export. The public identifiers and text fields are synthetic: video IDs, video titles, channel IDs, channel names, search queries, tags, and URLs have been replaced with deterministic fake values.

Included public data:

- `data/mock_takeout/`: mock donor files.
- `data/manual/unavailable_content_classification_filled.csv`: manual classification map for generalized availability/error messages.
- `data/demo_metadata/meta_data_public.csv`: scrambled video metadata fixture used for offline reproduction.

The public repository does not include real participant donations, private source Takeout exports, exploratory legacy notebooks, full scraped metadata with subtitle text or long descriptions, real YouTube video/channel identifiers, or temporary subtitle files.

Notebook 03 demonstrates the scraping procedure, but public readers should not need to scrape YouTube to understand the method. The scrambled metadata fixture allows notebook 04 and notebook 05 to run offline while preserving the shape of the original metadata workflow. The fake public video IDs are not intended to be scrapeable.
